Control Description: Develop, document, and disseminate a formal policy and procedures to manage system access
Current State: Policy exists but outdated and partially communicated to staff.
Desired State: Current, approved access control policies and procedures disseminated to all personnel; reviewed annually.
Gap: The organization does not have a formal process to regularly review, approve, and share the access control policy, which can lead to outdated information and inconsistent communication.
GAP Control Description: Implement a formal process to manage the access control policy that includes yearly reviews, leadership approval, version tracking, and required distribution to employees with confirmation that they’ve read it.
Gap Control Recommendation: AC-1, Supporting controls AT-2, PL-2, CA-7
Justification for Supporting Controls: AT-2 ensures staff awareness; PL-2 ensures policy maintenance; CA-7 ensures ongoing oversight

Control Description: Manage the full lifecycle of information system accounts—creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal—to prevent unauthorized access
Current State: Accounts created manually; no automated deprovisioning.
Desired State: Automated provisioning/deprovisioning with quarterly reviews and documented approvals.
Gap: User accounts are created manually with no automated setup or removal, and quarterly access reviews are not done consistently, increasing the risk of unauthorized access, unused accounts, and compliance issues.
GAP Control Description: Implement a automated processes to create and remove user accounts, require quarterly access reviews with formal approvals, and keep records showing how accounts are managed throughout their lifecycle.
Gap Control Recommendation: AC-2. Supporting Controls -AC-2(3), AC-2(4), AC-2(7), AU-2 & AU 6
Justification for Supporting Controls: AC-2(3)Automatically disable inactive or terminated accounts, AC-2(4)Conduct regular (e.g., quarterly) account reviews and document results, AU-2 -Log account creation/deactivation events & AU-6 - review logs to ensure compliance

Control Description: Requires information systems to enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and resources, aligning with organization-defined policies
Current State: RBAC partially applied; shared admin accounts exist.
Desired State: Access is controlled using strict role-based access, each user has their own account, shared admin accounts are not allowed, and permissions are managed centrally at the system level.
Gap: Role-based access is not applied consistently, shared admin accounts are in use, and access is not centrally managed, reducing accountability and weakening least-privilege controls.
GAP Control Description: Implemnt a centrally managed role-based access using individual user accounts, remove shared admin credentials, enforce least-privilege access, and standardize how access is controlled across systems.
Gap Control Recommendation: AC-3(7) Supporting Controls - AC-2, AC-5, AC-6 AC, IA-2, IA-5, CA-7
Justification for Supporting Controls: AC-2 ensures unique account ownership, AC-5 prevents privilege sharing, AC-6 enforces least privilege, IA-2 enforces individual authentication, IA-5 Protects administrative credentials, CA-7 ensures ongoing privilege oversight.

Control Description: To divide duty-related tasks among different individuals to prevent fraud, misuse, and errors
Current State: Some financial approval and travel booking tasks can be done by same user.
Desired State: Critical tasks are separated, and approvals require two people.
Gap: Some users can both approve financial transactions and book travel, which reduces separation of duties and increases the risk of fraud, mistakes, and unauthorized activity.
GAP Control Description: Create a clear chart that defines who is responsible for each task, and set up an approval process so duties are properly separated and controlled.
Gap Control Recommendation: AC-5 Supporting Controls - AC-3(2), AC-2, AC-6, AU-2/AU-6, CA-7
Justification for Supporting Controls: AC-3(2) enforces dual authorization; AC-2 Ensures unique accounts to prevent role overlap; AC-6 restricts privileges; AU-2/AU-6 Provides evidence that dual approvals occurred,  CA-7 monitors ongoing compliance with separation-of-duties policies.

Control Description: Organizational users and processes to be uniquely identified and authenticated before accessing information systems
Desired State: MFA for all users including administrators and remote access.
Gap: Access is currently protected only by passwords, which increases the risk of unauthorized entry to systems and sensitive data. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is not required for administrators or remote users, leaving accounts less secure.
GAP Control Description: Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all users, including administrators and remote users, so that logging in requires an extra verification step beyond just a password
Gap Control Recommendation: IA-2,  Supporting Controls - IA-5, AC-2, AC-17, AU-2/AU-6, CA-
Justification for Supporting Controls: IA-5 ensures MFA credentials are properly managed, AC-2 Ensures accounts are uniquely assigned to individuals to enable MFA enforcement,  AC-17 enforces MFA for remote access, AU-2 / AU-6 Provides evidence of authentication attempts and MFA compliance, CA-7 ensures ongoing MFA enforcement.

Current State: No formal password expiration or complexity enforcement.
Desired State: Strong password policy enforced; periodic password changes.
Gap: There are no rules requiring strong passwords or regular password changes, which increases the risk of weak or reused passwords being compromised and leading to unauthorized access.
GAP Control Description: Implement a strong password policy that requires complex passwords, regular updates, and secure handling of credentials for all users
Gap Control Recommendation: IA-5,  Supporting Controls - IA-2, AC-2, AC-6, AU-2/AU-6, CA-
Justification for Supporting Controls: IA-2 links credentials to unique users; AC-2 ensures unique account, AU-2/AU-6 Provides evidence of password policy compliance and authentication events, CA-7 monitors ongoing compliance with password requirements

Control Description: Identify, define, and document which events must be logged in their information systems to support security monitoring, investigations, and accountability
Current State: Basic logging; not all transactions logged.
Desired State: All financial and PII transactions logged; centralized log storage.
Gap: System logs are incomplete and do not track all financial and personal data activities. In addition, logs are not centrally collected, which limits visibility, accountability, and the ability to quickly detect incidents.
GAP Control Description: Impement full logging of all financial and personal data (PII) activity, and centralize audit logs with proper storage and retention to improve visibility, accountability, and incident detection
Gap Control Recommendation: AU-2, Supporting Controls - AU-3, AU-6, AU-9 , SI-4, CA-7
Justification for Supporting Controls: AU-3 ensures detailed audit records; AU-6 requires centralized log review; AU-9 protects logs from tampering; SI-4 enables monitoring; CA-7 ensures ongoing audit effectiveness.

Control Description: Regularly review and analyze audit logs and report suspicious activity.
Current State: Logs rarely reviewed unless incident occurs.
Desired State: Automated SIEM monitoring with weekly review and alerts for anomalies.
Gap: Audit logs are rarely reviewed unless an incident occurs, resulting in delayed detection of suspicious activity and weak proactive monitoring
GAP Control Description: Implement automated SIEM-based monitoring with defined alert thresholds and require scheduled weekly audit log reviews to detect anomalies and unauthorized activity
Gap Control Recommendation: AU-6, Supporting Controls - SI-4, AU-2, AU-12, IR-5, CA-7
Justification for Supporting Controls: SI-4 enables automated anomaly detection; AU-2 Ensures necessary security events are logged for SIEM ingestion, AU-12 Ensures systems consistently generate logs for analysis, IR-5 connects alerts to incident response, CA-7 ensures continuous monitoring oversight

Control Description: Systems must generate audit records with accurate, synchronized time stamps
Desired State: Network Time Protocol (NTP) used; all logs time-synced.
Gap: System clocks are not synchronized, causing inconsistent timestamps that reduce the reliability and correlation of audit logs.
GAP Control Description: Implement centralized Network Time Protocol (NTP) synchronization across all systems to ensure consistent, accurate timestamps in audit logs.
Gap Control Recommendation: AU-8, Supporting Controls - AU-12, AU-6, SI-4, SC-45, CA-7
Justification for Supporting Controls: AU-12 ensures logs contain synchronized timestamps, AU-6 enables accurate log correlation, SI-4 Requires consistent time for event detection accuracy, SC-45 enforces trusted time sources, CA-7 ensures ongoing synchronization oversight

Control Description: Monitor, control, and protect communications at external and internal network boundaries.
Current State: Basic firewall deployed; no internal segmentation.
Desired State: Network segmentation implemented; IDS/IPS monitoring traffic.
Gap: Network protection relies on a basic perimeter firewall without internal segmentation or intrusion monitoring, increasing the risk of lateral movement and undetected malicious activity.
GAP Control Description: Implement internal network segmentation and deploy IDS/IPS monitoring to enforce traffic boundaries and detect unauthorized or malicious activity.
Gap Control Recommendation: SC-7, Supporting Controls - SI-4, SC-5, IA-3, CA-7
Justification for Supporting Controls: SI-4 enables network monitoring, SC-5 strengthens bL13oundary resilience, IA-3 restricts unauthorized devices,  CA-7 ensures ongoing boundary protection oversight

Control Description: Securely establish and manage cryptographic keys used for encryption.
Current State: Ad-hoc key rotation; keys stored locally.
Desired State: Formal key management and rotation; keys stored in HSM or secure KMS.
Gap: Cryptographic keys are rotated inconsistently and stored locally without formal management controls, increasing the risk of key compromise and loss of cryptographic integrity
GAP Control Description: Implement a formal cryptographic key management program with defined rotation schedules and store keys in a hardware security module (HSM) or secure centralized key management service (KMS)
Gap Control Recommendation: SC-12, Supporting Controls - IA-7, SC-28, KM-1, SI-7, CA-7
Justification for Supporting Controls: IA-7 protects access to cryptographic modules; SC-28 ensures encrypted data depends on protected keys; KM-1 formalizes key governance; SI-7 detects key tampering; CA-7 ensures ongoing compliance.

Control Description: Use approved cryptographic methods to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information.
Current State: Data at rest encrypted; partial encryption in transit.
Desired State: TLS 1.2+ enforced; all sensitive data encrypted in transit and at rest.
Gap: Encryption is applied inconsistently, with informal key management and no standard requirement for protecting data in transit or at rest. This increases the risk of sensitive data being exposed
GAP Control Description: Require strong encryption for all data in transit (TLS 1.2 or higher) and ensure sensitive data at rest is encrypted using standardized, centrally managed cryptographic controls.
Gap Control Recommendation: SC-13, Supporting Controls - SC-12, SC-28, SC-16 , IA-7, CA-7
Justification for Supporting Controls: SC-12 protects encryption keys; SC-28 enforces data-at-rest encryption; SC-16 secures transmission integrity; IA-7 Restricts access to cryptographic modules; CA-7 ensures ongoing encryption compliance

Control Description: Identify, report, and correct system flaws in a timely manner.
Desired State: Automated patching with defined timelines for high and critical findings.
Gap: Patch management is performed manually without defined remediation timelines, resulting in inconsistent vulnerability remediation and increased exposure to exploitation.
GAP Control Description: Implement an automated patch management process with defined service level agreements (SLAs) for remediation of high and critical vulnerabilities.
Gap Control Recommendation: SI-2, Supporting Controls - RA-5, CM-3, CM-6, SI-4, CA-7
Justification for Supporting Controls: RA-5 identifies vulnerabilities, CM-3 governs patch changes, CM-6 enforces secure baselines, SI-4 detects potential exploitation activity, CA-7 Tracks remediation effectiveness.

Control Description: Regularly scan systems for vulnerabilities and analyze results to reduce risk.
Desired State: Automated scanning with documented remediation and management reporting.
Gap: Vulnerability scans are performed monthly, but tracking is informal, making it hard to clearly see remediation progress. This leads to inconsistent follow-up and limited management oversight.
GAP Control Description: Implement automated vulnerability scanning and track all findings in a central system. Set clear remediation deadlines and provide regular reports to management on vulnerability status and trends.
Gap Control Recommendation: RA-5, Supporting Controls - SI-2, CA-7, AU-6, CM-3, PM-6
Justification for Supporting Controls: SI-2 enforces remediation timelines, CA-7 ensures continuous oversight, AU-6 Supports reporting and analysis of scan results, CM-3 governs patch changes, PM-6 Enables executive-level metrics and reporting.

Control Description: Create, protect, and test system backups so data and systems can be restored when needed.
Desired State: Daily encrypted backups; quarterly restoration tests; RPO/RTO documented.
Gap: Daily backups are performed, but they are not encrypted, recovery testing is not documented, and key recovery targets (RPO and RTO) are not defined. This increases the risk of data exposure and failed recovery during an incident
GAP Control Description: Implement encrypted daily backups, perform and document regular restoration testing (at least quarterly), and formally define and approve Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) and Recovery Time Objectives (RTO).
Gap Control Recommendation: CP-9, Supporting Controls - CP-10, SC-28, SC-12, CA-7, IR-4
Justification for Supporting Controls: CP-10 Ensures systems can be restored after disruption, SC-28 enforces backup encryption, SC-12 secures backup keys, CA-7 monitors backup compliance, IR-4 integrates recovery into incident response.

Control Description: Implement and maintain a capability to handle security incidents effectively.
Current State: Generic IR plan; no financial fraud or PII scenarios.
Desired State: Documented IR procedures for PII, financial fraud, and credit card compromise; annual tabletop exercises.
Gap: The Incident Response Plan is generic and does not include documented procedures for PII breaches, financial fraud, or credit card compromise. Additionally, incident response procedures are not validated through regular tabletop exercises.
GAP Control Description: Develop and document detailed incident response procedures for PII breaches, financial fraud, and credit card compromise, and conduct annual tabletop exercises to validate response effectiveness.
Gap Control Recommendation: IR-4, Supporting Controls - IR-2, IR-3, IR-6, SI-4, CP-2
Justification for Supporting Controls: IR-2 Ensures staff are trained, IR-3 Validates procedures through exercises, IR-6 Governs internal/external breach notifications, SI-4 Detects incidents requiring response, CP-2 Aligns recovery procedures with IR activities.

Control Description: Define, document, implement, and enforce secure configuration settings for systems.
Current State: IT states baseline exists; not formally documented or monitored.
Desired State: Documented secure baseline configurations; monitored for drift; deviations logged.
Gap: Secure configuration settings are said to be in place, but they are not formally documented, approved, or continuously checked for changes. This increases the risk of unauthorized or insecure system configurations
GAP Control Description: Create and approve documented secure baseline configurations, and use automated tools to continuously monitor and alert on any configuration changes or deviations.
Gap Control Recommendation: CM-4, Supporting Controls - CM-2, CM-3, CM-6, CA-7, AU-12
Justification for Supporting Controls: CM-2 Formalizes baseline documentation, CM-3 Governs approval of configuration changes, CM-6 Ensures secure settings are consistently applied, CA-7 Requires ongoing monitoring of configuration compliance, AU-12 Logs configuration changes and deviations.

Control Description: Configure systems to provide only essential capabilities and disable unnecessary features.
Current State: Some unused services and protocols enabled.
Desired State: Disable unnecessary services; minimal functionality enforced.
Gap: Some systems have unused or unnecessary services and protocols enabled, increasing the attack surface and potential for exploitation. Least functionality is not enforced.
GAP Control Description: Identify and disable all unnecessary services, protocols, and features; enforce minimal functionality consistent with operational requirements and document approved exceptions.
Gap Control Recommendation: CM-7, Supporting Controls - CM-6, CM-2, SI-6, SC-7, CA-7
Justification for Supporting Controls: CM-6 enforces minimal functionality, CM-2 Establishes a secure baseline reflecting only required services; SI-7 Detect if something unauthorized gets added or changed, SC-7 Limits external access to only necessary services, CA-7 Ensures minimal functionality is maintained over time.

Control Description: Identify, track, and maintain an inventory of all system components.
Current State: Inventory partially documented; missing software versions.
Desired State: Comprehensive inventory of hardware and software maintained and regularly updated.
Gap: The organization maintains only a partial inventory of information system components, with missing software versions, reducing visibility and increasing the risk of unmanaged or vulnerable assets.
GAP Control Description: Develop and maintain a comprehensive, centralized inventory of all hardware and software components, including versions, and implement a process for regular updates and verification.
Gap Control Recommendation: CM-8, Supporting Controls - CM-2, CM-3, CM-6
Justification for Supporting Controls: CM-2 Ensures inventory reflects secure baselines, CM-3 Updates inventory with changes, CM-6 Ensures system configurations are consistent with inventory records
